title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government responds to the Committee's 2020 report on artificial intelligence and public standards, outlining its plans to strengthen AI governance, transparency, and accountability. It proposes new policies, regulatory measures, and collaborative efforts to ensure AI systems are aligned with public interest and safety.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will monitor and guide the use of artificial intelligence in exams and qualifications. The aim is to keep testing fair, transparent and secure while also encouraging responsible innovation in the sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report reviews how using copyrighted works influences the creation and training of AI systems, looking at legal, ethical, and technical issues. It evaluates the potential impacts on creators, users, and the AI industry, and offers guidance on balancing innovation with copyright protection.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government outlines its strategy to address the committee’s recommendations on AI, focusing on boosting research, protecting public safety, and ensuring the UK remains a leader in ethical AI development. It pledges to increase funding, strengthen regulation, and collaborate with industry and academia to foster innovation while safeguarding jobs and privacy.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the responsibilities and scope of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence interacts with public standards. It also includes frequently asked questions to clarify the committee’s objectives, processes, and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission outlines the company’s perspective on key AI policy issues and proposes recommendations for improving governance frameworks.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy examines how artificial intelligence will shape the rules and standards for medical products, ensuring they remain safe and effective. It outlines steps for integrating the key principles from the AI White Paper into existing regulatory frameworks, promoting transparency, accountability, and patient protection.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the defence organisation the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential user of AI for its size. By adopting advanced AI technologies, it will strengthen operational capabilities, streamline processes and enhance national security while upholding high ethical and trust standards.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport sector to harness AI’s benefits while addressing its risks. It outlines practical steps for implementing AI safely and responsibly across the industry.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This document reports on how copyright-protected works are being used in training and developing AI systems, focusing on the legal framework set out in Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It provides updates on compliance, challenges, and future steps to ensure that AI development respects copyright law while encouraging innovation.
